layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tents are higher than 1.O mM.This spatial partitioning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of sulphate and methane lead to the earlier postulation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a noncommensurate behaviour between sulphate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reducing and methanogenic bacteria. In contrast to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the early resuIts of BARBER(1974),CAPPENBERG(1974)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and WINFREY and ZEIKUs(1977) showing methano-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: genesis inhibition by sulphate,mutual coexistence has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been demonstrated by LAWRENCE et al.(1964), LAW-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RENCE and McCARTY (1965),POLCIN et al. (1981)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and LovLEY et al. (1982).Methanogenesis in some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: freshwater environments is reported by CAPPENBERG

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1975）to be inhibited by the relatively low sulphide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: activities.HoWever,INGVORSEN and BROCK(1982)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have shown that methane and suiphide can coexist,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and MAH et al.(1977) reported that sulphide in certain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instances can actually stimulate methanogenesis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fermentation is regarded by many investigators as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: major source of methane (about 7O%） in freshwater

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments,such as sediments (KoYAMA，1964:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TAKAI,1970; BELYAEV et al.,1975;WINFREY et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1977；CAPPENBERG and JONGEJAN，1978)； sewage

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sludges (JERIS and McCARTY,1965; SMITHand MAH,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1966;MOUNTFORT and AsHER,1978) and in numer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ous culture studies (CAPPENBERG and PRINS,1974;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: WEIMER and ZEIKUS,1978; ZINDER and MAH,1979;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SMITH and MAH,1978,1980).As mentioned before

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: there is evidence,however, that other substrates may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be important,and that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduction can be the pri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marymethane source in certain low sulphate freshwater

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments such as hot-spring algal mats (SANDBECK

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and WARD, 1981) and in bovine rumen (OPPERMANN

layout_dets.text: ISOTOPE VARIATIONS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Schematically depicted in Fig.1, the methyl position

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of acetate in anoxic freshwater sediments is fermented

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to methane.The carbon dioxide released by this acetate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dissimilation may also be reduced to methane,though

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perhaps on a diminished scale.This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could continue to operate even after acetate is ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hausted and the acetate fermentation pathway ceases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The mode of methane generation is somewhat dif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferent in the saline environments such as salt marshes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and marine sediments (Fig.1). Based on culture studies,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the reduction of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by hydrogen is considered here

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be the dominant pathway for bacterial methane for-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation (BELYAEV et al., 1977; OREMLAND and TAY-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stimulation of methanogenesis by hydrogen addition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been demonstrated by MYLROIE and HUNGATE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1955), OREMLAND and TAYLOR (1978),WINFREY and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ZEIKUS (1977) and ABRAM and NEDWELL (1978a,b).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This hydrogen addition was shown by WINFREY et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1977） to increase methane production via

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duction but had no effect on the fermentation rate.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Although both methane production pathways can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operate in freshwater and marine sediments,the rel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ative proportions of each pathway are variable and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controlled by the availability of substrates and hydro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen to the methanogens,which in turn can be limited

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by competition from sulphate reducing bacteria.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These pathways of biogenic methane formation can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be further substantiated by the use of carbon and hy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: drogen isotopes.As discussed next, the combination

layout_dets.text: sediments on methane with the coexisting

layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.text: produce distinctive fractionations which can de-
